skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate and edit AI videos through the inference.sh belt CLI using model examples for text-to-video, image-to-video, lipsync, upscaling, foley, and clip merging.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh video model workflows from clear belt CLI examples.
skill.author: inference-sh-skills

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick and hardcoded URL findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, fenced command examples, model IDs, and documentation links. No prompt injection or hidden malicious behavior was found in SKILL.md. The remaining concern is expected external processing of prompts and media URLs through the inference.sh belt CLI.

remediation.suggestion: Add a clear note that prompts, image URLs, audio URLs, and video URLs may be processed by inference.sh and model providers.
Ask for confirmation before long, high-resolution, or repeated video jobs, especially after belt login.
Tell users to replace placeholder URLs with media they own or have permission to use.

semantic_findings.title: External Media Processing Disclosure Needed
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to run the belt CLI against inference.sh video apps. Example workflows accept image, audio, and video URLs, so users may send personal media to external providers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed belt CLI use and documented image, audio, and video URL examples show intended external processing. The risk is disclosed by context but should be explicit for private media.

content.value_statement: Choosing the right video model and CLI input can slow production. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear inference.sh video workflows.
actual_capabilities: Recommends model IDs for text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video, lipsync, editing, upscaling, foley, and merging.
Shows belt CLI examples for Google Veo, Seedance, Wan, Grok, OmniHuman, Fabric, and other video apps.
Supports browsing available video apps with the video category command.
Covers input fields such as prompt, duration, resolution, image URL, audio URL, and video URL.
Links related skills for avatars, narration, image generation, and social posting.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Video jobs may use external services and account credits.
Sample media URLs are placeholders and must be replaced.
The skill does not list current prices, quotas, or provider content rules.

use_cases.title: Create Social Clips
use_cases.description: Generate short videos from prompts or images for posts, campaigns, and tests.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Videos
use_cases.description: Select model examples for explainer clips, product motion, or background changes.

use_cases.title: Build Video Pipelines
use_cases.description: Combine generation, upscaling, foley, and clip merging through repeatable CLI steps.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Short Prompt Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-video-generation to create a five second text-to-video clip about [scene]. Recommend the best fast model and ask before running.

prompt_templates.title: Animate an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-video-generation to turn [image URL] into a short video. Include motion guidance, duration, and a safe model choice.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Talking Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-video-generation with [portrait URL] and [audio URL] to prepare a lipsync or avatar workflow. Explain privacy checks first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Step Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-video-generation to plan a pipeline for [goal] with generation, upscaling, foley, and merging. Compare model choices before any command.

output_examples.input: I need a five second product teaser from a text prompt.
output_examples.output: Recommended workflow: use a fast text-to-video model first, then upscale only if the result is approved. Confirm prompt, duration, and credit use.

output_examples.input: Animate a product image and add natural sound.
output: Recommended first step: use an image-to-video model for motion.
Recommended second step: add foley sound after the motion clip is approved.
Required input: a user-owned image URL.

output_examples.input: Create a talking head from a portrait and audio.
output_examples.output: Recommended workflow: confirm media rights, choose an avatar or lipsync model, then submit portrait and audio URLs through the belt CLI.

best_practices: Confirm media rights before using portraits, voices, product footage, or branded assets.
Start with fast or economical models before requesting high resolution output.
Review prompts, durations, and URLs before running jobs that may use credits.
anti_patterns: Do not run generation jobs with private media unless external processing is approved.
Do not leave placeholder URLs in requests.
Do not request maximum duration or resolution before testing the prompt.

faq.question: Does this skill require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the inference.sh belt CLI and a logged-in account.

faq.question: Can it generate videos from text?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes text-to-video examples for several supported video models.

faq.question: Can it animate an image?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes image-to-video and reference-to-video model examples.

faq.question: Will my media leave my environment?
faq.answer: Yes, when jobs run. Prompts and media URLs are sent to inference.sh or selected providers.

faq.question: Does it choose the cheapest model?
faq.answer: It lists economical options, but it does not include current prices or quotas.

faq.question: Can it post videos to social networks?
faq.answer: It links a related social posting skill, but this skill focuses on video generation and editing.
